11:39.sourceText: εἶπεν δὲ ὁ Κύριος πρὸς αὐτόν Νῦν ὑμεῖς οἱ Φαρισαῖοι τὸ ἔξωθεν τοῦ ποτηρίου καὶ τοῦ πίνακος καθαρίζετε, τὸ δὲ ἔσωθεν ὑμῶν γέμει ἁρπαγῆς καὶ πονηρίας.
11:39.targetText: And the LORD said to him, “Now you, the Pharisees, make the outside of the cup and of the plate clean, but your inward part is full of robbery and wickedness.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

11:40.sourceText: ἄφρονες, οὐχ ὁ ποιήσας τὸ ἔξωθεν καὶ τὸ ἔσωθεν ἐποίησεν;
11:40.targetText: Unthinking [ones]! Did He who made the outside not also make the inside?

11:41.sourceText: πλὴν τὰ ἐνόντα δότε ἐλεημοσύνην, καὶ ἰδοὺ πάντα καθαρὰ ὑμῖν ἐστιν.
11:41.targetText: But what you have given [as] alms, and behold, all things are clean to you.

groups.note: Actual τὰ ἐνόντα denotes the things within/on hand. English what you have is its possessions/available-contents rendering, not a separately written Greek have verb; the alternative literal within wording remains visible.
Actual δότε is the active plural imperative give. Exact LSV prints given; this English wording is preserved without changing the source imperative into a participle or a completed-giving form.

review.note: The actual within/on-hand constituent and imperative give are retained despite the unusual exact LSV word order and given wording. This is a grammar/rendering note, not an interpretation of what the inward things signify.

11:42.sourceText: ἀλλὰ οὐαὶ ὑμῖν τοῖς Φαρισαίοις, ὅτι ἀποδεκατοῦτε τὸ ἡδύοσμον καὶ τὸ πήγανον καὶ πᾶν λάχανον, καὶ παρέρχεσθε τὴν κρίσιν καὶ τὴν ἀγάπην τοῦ Θεοῦ· ταῦτα δὲ ἔδει ποιῆσαι κἀκεῖνα μὴ παρεῖναι.
11:42.targetText: But woe to you, the Pharisees, because you tithe the mint, and the rue, and every herb, and you pass by the judgment and the love of God; these things [you] should do, and those not to be neglecting.

groups.note: Actual ἔδει is the impersonal it-was-necessary/ought predicate, rendered should. No separately written Greek personal you subject is claimed.

unmappedSource.reason: Actual δέ marks a transition to the obligation statement; LSV uses a punctuation break without separately rendering this connector.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a personal subject to the impersonal ought/necessity construction. Pinned N1904 has no independently printed personal subject word here.

11:43.sourceText: οὐαὶ ὑμῖν τοῖς Φαρισαίοις, ὅτι ἀγαπᾶτε τὴν πρωτοκαθεδρίαν ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς καὶ τοὺς ἀσπασμοὺς ἐν ταῖς ἀγοραῖς.
11:43.targetText: Woe to you, the Pharisees, because you love the first seats in the synagogues and the salutations in the marketplaces.

groups.note: Actual πρωτοκαθεδρία is the chief-seat/front-seat noun, singular in Greek and rendered first seats in English. No independent Greek first numeral or plural source inflection is claimed.

11:44.sourceText: οὐαὶ ὑμῖν, ὅτι ἐστὲ ὡς τὰ μνημεῖα τὰ ἄδηλα, καὶ οἱ ἄνθρωποι οἱ περιπατοῦντες ἐπάνω οὐκ οἴδασιν.
11:44.targetText: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you are as the unseen tombs, and the men walking above have not known.”

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.
Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

unmappedTarget.reason: The longer witness names the scribes/Pharisees and hypocrites as the woe’s addressees. Pinned N1904 has only woe to you before the because clause.

11:45.sourceText: Ἀποκριθεὶς δέ τις τῶν νομικῶν λέγει αὐτῷ Διδάσκαλε, ταῦτα λέγων καὶ ἡμᾶς ὑβρίζεις.
11:45.targetText: And one of the lawyers answering, says to Him, “Teacher, saying these things, You also insult us”;

11:46.sourceText: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν Καὶ ὑμῖν τοῖς νομικοῖς οὐαί, ὅτι φορτίζετε τοὺς ἀνθρώπους φορτία δυσβάστακτα, καὶ αὐτοὶ ἑνὶ τῶν δακτύλων ὑμῶν οὐ προσψαύετε τοῖς φορτίοις.
11:46.targetText: and He said, “And to you, the lawyers, woe! Because you burden men with burdens [too] grievous to bear, and you yourselves do not touch the burdens with one of your fingers.

groups.note: Actual φορτία is the accusative burden object of burden/load. English with burdens realizes that same loaded-object relation, not a separately written Greek with preposition.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

11:47.sourceText: οὐαὶ ὑμῖν, ὅτι οἰκοδομεῖτε τὰ μνημεῖα τῶν προφητῶν, οἱ δὲ πατέρες ὑμῶν ἀπέκτειναν αὐτούς.
11:47.targetText: Woe to you, because you build the tombs of the prophets, and your fathers killed them.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

11:48.sourceText: ἄρα μάρτυρές ἐστε καὶ συνευδοκεῖτε τοῖς ἔργοις τῶν πατέρων ὑμῶν, ὅτι αὐτοὶ μὲν ἀπέκτειναν αὐτοὺς, ὑμεῖς δὲ οἰκοδομεῖτε.
11:48.targetText: Then you testify, and are well pleased with the works of your fathers, because they indeed killed them, and you build their tombs;

groups.note: Actual μάρτυρές ἐστε is the nominal you-are-witnesses predicate. English verbalizes that same witness relation as you testify; no separately printed Greek testify verb is claimed.

unmappedTarget.reason: The longer witness explicitly supplies the tomb object and its personal possessive after build. Pinned N1904 has the build predicate without a written object here; the tombs are understood from the preceding sentence, not newly printed source words.

11:49.sourceText: διὰ τοῦτο καὶ ἡ σοφία τοῦ Θεοῦ εἶπεν Ἀποστελῶ εἰς αὐτοὺς προφήτας καὶ ἀποστόλους, καὶ ἐξ αὐτῶν ἀποκτενοῦσιν καὶ διώξουσιν,
11:49.targetText: because of this also the wisdom of God said: I will send to them prophets, and apostles, and some of them they will kill and persecute,

groups.note: Actual ἐξ αὐτῶν is the partitive out-of-them phrase. English some makes its selected-members object explicit; no independent Greek some noun/pronoun is printed.

11:50.sourceText: ἵνα ἐκζητηθῇ τὸ αἷμα πάντων τῶν προφητῶν τὸ ἐκκεχυμένον ἀπὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου ἀπὸ τῆς γενεᾶς ταύτης,
11:50.targetText: that the blood of all the prophets, that is being poured forth from the foundation of the world, may be required from this generation—

groups.note: Actual ἐκκεχυμένον is perfect passive poured-out, rendered is being poured forth. The actual perfect participle is retained, not relabeled as a present-progressive Greek form.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

11:51.sourceText: ἀπὸ αἵματος Ἄβελ ἕως αἵματος Ζαχαρίου τοῦ ἀπολομένου μεταξὺ τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου καὶ τοῦ οἴκου· ναί, λέγω ὑμῖν, ἐκζητηθήσεται ἀπὸ τῆς γενεᾶς ταύτης.
11:51.targetText: from the blood of Abel to the blood of Zacharias, who perished between the altar and the house; yes, I say to you, it will be required from this generation.

11:52.sourceText: οὐαὶ ὑμῖν τοῖς νομικοῖς, ὅτι ἤρατε τὴν κλεῖδα τῆς γνώσεως· αὐτοὶ οὐκ εἰσήλθατε καὶ τοὺς εἰσερχομένους ἐκωλύσατε.
11:52.targetText: Woe to you, the lawyers, because you took away the key of the knowledge; you yourselves did not enter; and you hindered those coming in.”

11:53.sourceText: Κἀκεῖθεν ἐξελθόντος αὐτοῦ ἤρξαντο οἱ γραμματεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι δεινῶς ἐνέχειν καὶ ἀποστοματίζειν αὐτὸν περὶ πλειόνων,
11:53.targetText: And in His speaking these things to them, the scribes and the Pharisees began fearfully to urge and to press Him to speak about many things,

groups.note: Actual κἀκεῖθεν fuses and plus from-there. LSV retains only the conjunction while replacing the whole departure circumstance; no English counterpart for its local from-there component is claimed.

Actual genitive αὐτοῦ is the personal subject of the departure genitive absolute. LSV uses the same person as subject of its different speaking circumstance; the person correspondence does not equate the unlike departure and speech predicates.

unmappedSource.reason: Actual ἐξελθόντος states his going out/departing from there. The LSV circumstance instead states his speaking these things to them, a different witness clause with no corresponding departure predicate.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV introduces a speaking-time circumstance with in, while pinned N1904 has a departure genitive absolute, not this temporal preposition.
The longer witness states a speaking circumstance with its content and recipients. Pinned N1904 instead states departure from there, without these speech/content/recipient words.
